title: Inhibiting Effects of Taurine on Doxorubicin-Induced Oxidative Stress in Rats

sections.abstract: <jats:p>The study was designed to observethe protective effect of taurine(Tau) against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in rats.Doxorubicin were administered at the dosage of 2.5 mg·kg<jats:sup>-1</jats:sup> oncea week, ip for a period of 4 consecutive weeks. Taurine were administered atthe dosages of400,200and 100 mg·kg<jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>·d<jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>, poby gavage for 30 consecutive days. Taurine at the doses of 400 and 200 mg·kg<jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>significantly reduced CK-MB, GOT and LDH and increased SOD levelsin the doxorubicin-treated animals. Thus, taurine ameliorated doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by reducingoxidative stress, abnormal cellular morphology in rat. The study show the protective effect oftaurine against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity.</jats:p>
